findings.statement: Marketing had the largest overspend at 152,200, spending 643,200 against a budget of 491,000.
findings.method: SQL join and subtraction to calculate overspend per department
findings.code: SELECT b.department, b.budget, a.actual, (a.actual - b.budget) AS overspend FROM budget_2025_budget b JOIN budget_2025_actual a ON b.department = a.department ORDER BY overspend DESC

data_quality_notes: No null values in either table
No duplicate rows in either table
All departments have matching entries between budget and actual tables
Data types are consistent: department as string, budget/actual as integers
assumptions: Budget and actual spending are for the same fiscal year 2025
Each department appears exactly once in both tables
Overspend is calculated as actual minus budget (positive = overspent)
limitations: Only 8 departments are included in the dataset
No information about the time period covered by the budget and actual figures
Cannot determine if overspending was intentional or due to external factors
